description: The house pipeline: seven CPU-only services (ingest, persons, tracker, faces, embed, match) conducted by a runner, with per-run galleries, staff enrolment and operator corrections.

persons.note: The stronger arm: 640-squared input, ~5x nano's compute — measured 147 ms/frame on a laptop CPU, which is why its home is the CUDA box. Same family, same decode path; a models.lock row away on any box.

Declared ahead of its weights, deliberately: the service speaks the rtdetr family contract (two-input export, no NMS) and models-restricted.lock documents why no pin exists yet (no official ONNX asset — needs a reproducible local export). An install that has not fetched it simply refuses profiles naming it, which is the M-mode-1 truth.

provenance.note: InsightFace lineage — non-commercial weights; grant purchasable, provenance disclosed (doc 07)

faces.note: The light arm of the family; restricted tier. Weights: InsightFace buffalo_m.zip (GitHub release v0.7) member det_2.5g.onnx, sha256 041f73f47371333d1d17a6fee6c8ab4e6aecabefe398ff32cca4e2d5eaee0af9 — the same pack family as scrfd-10g (buffalo_l det_10g.onnx, byte-identical to the box's scrfd_10g_kps.onnx); 9-tensor *_kps export, dynamic input, loads at 640 and 1472x832. Measured 2026-09-24 on the 4060, 8 frames of the Sharon bench clip, session.run vs scrfd-10g: 640 CUDA 3.8 vs 7.5 ms (TensorRT 1.7 vs 2.5); 1472x832 CUDA 8.2 vs 20.4 ms (TensorRT 3.6 vs 5.3). It pays in recall: at scoreMin 0.7 it kept 5 of scrfd-10g's 6 faces at 640 and 14 of 17 at 1472x832 (one lost face was 173 px wide). Its place is a CUDA-only box whose GPU budget binds; where TensorRT runs, scrfd-10g at 1472x832 is both faster than this on CUDA and keeps those faces.

provenance.note: InsightFace lineage — non-commercial weights; grant purchasable, provenance disclosed (doc 07)

faces.note: The 10G arm of the same family — ~4x 2.5g's compute, same 9-tensor *_kps decode, and detector.py's MODEL_SPECS already knew the filename. Declared because the CUDA box RUNS it: an install whose live model is undeclared refuses every profile naming it, which is the model gate doing its job and also the one way to make a working stack unlaunchable. Its home is a GPU — on a CPU box it is the wrong end of the family.

calibration.note: the paper's 1:1 operating point plus bench-measured bands; venue calibration is the M3 gap

provenance.note: WebFace600K lineage — the permanent face-stage disclosure (doc 07: not curable by purchase)

calibration.note: evaluation-only until eval/sweep.py writes it a pack from our labels; per-embedder staff store + HECO_EMBEDDING_DIM=512 travel with any deployment of it

embed.note: The generic-embedder path proven by the arcface family (own alignment, dim read from the graph). NOT hot-swappable by design — an embedder change is a deployment (doc 15 M3).

provenance.note: no implementation loaded — long-term identity is the gallery's job (docs/planning/02, core design principle)

notes: The reference pipeline, so its weight is 1.0 by definition and every other rate is read against it.

identityScope is split per docs/planning/15-model-configurations.md §12.4: guests are `run`-scoped (a fresh gallery-<runId>.db per run, swept at HECO_GALLERY_RETENTION_S — a returning guest at next month's event is a new billable guest) and staff are `venue`-scoped (the consented staff-<siteId>.db persists, with the tombstone erasure flow attached).

The `models` block is the open catalog's declaration (docs/planning/15-model-configurations.md §3): what this install can run per stage, with grant and provenance carried as separate fields because the grant is purchasable and the provenance is not. Today it declares exactly the models that have always run; restricted entries arrive with M2.
The run's config stamps which models actually RAN (asked of each service's /health at start) — the catalog declares what is offerable, the stamp records what happened.
